title: review: daemon dispatch: a render error on the main execute path must hold the task visibly (R22 gap)
spec:
Observed 2026-09-22 14:12Z on T-0773: its spec quoted literal double-brace placeholders, so spawn.render("execute", ...) raised ValueError unfilled_placeholder inside daemon.dispatch's main loop (daemon.py ~853-856: `packet = spawn.packet(...)`, `prompt = spawn.render("execute", ...)`, `spawn_async(_dispatch_worker, ...)`, `complete(t["id"], "dispatched_at")`). The exception escaped the per-task block: dispatched_at stayed stamped, no event, no hold, the task sat "queued" and was silently re-attempted every lease (three memory-recall rows, no execute rows). R22 (T-0755/T-0757) added render-error holds for _dispatch_fresh_fix and spawn.run_worker but not this path.
Do: wrap the packet build + render + spawn_async of the main execute dispatch path in try/except; on exception call hold_failed(t["id"], "dispatch_error", "dispatch", e) (existing helper at daemon.py ~484) so the task is held with hold_reason "dispatch failed: ValueError" and pipeline.dispatch_error carries the message, never leaving dispatched_at stamped on a task that did not launch (clear it in the same locked update). Also make _dispatch_worker (daemon.py ~496-535) handle every executor.start status: "held"/"budget" → clear dispatched_at and set status queued with pipeline.hold_note (held) so the next tick retries; "refused"/"incompatible" → post_result failed with the reason; "fallback" → leave as is (the Claude worker owns the task). Today only done/failed are handled and any other status leaves the task queued with dispatched_at stamped.
Tests (unittest): tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_render_error_holds_task (an execute task whose spec contains a literal double-brace token: after one tick the task is held with hold_reason starting "dispatch failed" and pipeline.dispatch_error mentions unfilled_placeholder; dispatched_at is not set), tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_worker_handles_non_terminal_start_statuses (executor.start patched to return {"status": "held", ...} then {"status": "refused", "reason": "x"}: first leaves the task queued without dispatched_at and with a hold_note, second posts a failed result with the reason). Keep all existing daemon tests green.

result.summary: Verified by running the full test suite in the T-0801 worktree (`python3 -m unittest tests.test_daemon`): all 209 tests pass, including the two new acceptance tests (test_dispatch_render_error_holds_task, test_dispatch_worker_handles_non_terminal_start_statuses) and the pre-existing test_dispatch_worker_leaves_held. The dispatch() try/except correctly wraps packet build + render + spawn_async and only stamps dispatched_at after that block succeeds; hold_failed's conditional pop of dispatched_at is scoped to error_key=='dispatch_error' and doesn't affect the other three callers (spec_review_error, gated_error, merged_error). _dispatch_worker now handles held/budget (requeue + hold_note, clearing dispatched_at), refused/incompatible (post failed result), and fallback (no-op) exactly as specified. No security concerns for this control-flow-only change to internal dispatch retry logic.
